ops.name: Owner
ops.description: Business owner who reviews overall financial health and trends.

ops.name: Bookkeeper
ops.description: Maintains the source spreadsheets and updates monthly figures.

ops.name: Manager
ops.description: Department lead who views budgets and actuals for their area.

ops.name: Accountant
ops.description: External advisor who reviews numbers at period close.

ops.name: Monthly Financials
ops.description: A month's summary of income, expenses, and profit pulled from the spreadsheet.

ops.name: Revenue Line
ops.description: A single income category for a period.

ops.name: Expense Line
ops.description: A single cost category for a period.

ops.name: Budget
ops.description: Planned amount for a category over a period.

ops.name: Department
ops.description: A part of the business that owns certain budgets and costs.
ops.example: Sales, managed by J. Rivera, CC-200

ops.name: Cash Balance
ops.description: Running cash position as of a date.

ops.name: KPI
ops.description: A tracked metric shown on the dashboard.

ops.name: Spreadsheet Import
ops.description: A record of an uploaded Excel file and when it was loaded.

ops.example: Owner checks gross margin against target
Manager reviews Marketing budget vs actuals
Owner sets Q2 Marketing budget to $16,000
Accountant reviews March figures at close
Accountant downloads March summary as Excel
Owner compares gross margin across quarters

ops.text: Only the Owner and Bookkeeper may upload or edit spreadsheet figures; Managers and Accountant see read-only views.
ops.example: A Manager cannot change an Expense Line amount.

ops.text: Each Manager may only view budgets and costs for their own Department.
ops.example: The Sales manager cannot open Operations department costs.

ops.text: A month's financials cannot be finalized until income and expense lines are both present.
ops.example: March cannot close while expenses are blank.

ops.text: Net profit must always equal total income minus total expenses for the same month.
Uploading a new spreadsheet for an already-loaded month replaces the prior figures and keeps a record of both uploads.
ops.example: Re-uploading March keeps the Apr 2 and Apr 5 import records.

ops.text: All amounts are shown in a single currency (USD) and no mixed currencies are allowed.
ops.example: A EUR figure would be rejected on import.

ops.text: Historical months cannot be edited once the Accountant marks them reviewed.
ops.example: Once March is reviewed, its lines lock.

ops.text: Does not send or generate customer invoices.
Does not connect directly to bank accounts or accounting software.
Does not run payroll or process payments.
Does not forecast or project future financials automatically.

A Department cannot be deleted while it still has linked Budgets or Expense Lines assigned to it.

ops.question: Who needs an account to use the app?

options.label: Nobody logs in — one person uses it on their own device
Exactly one person logs in (the owner)
Several people log in, possibly with different powers

ops.question: Do different people have different powers?

options.label: Everyone who logs in can do everything
An owner/admin plus staff with fewer powers
Admins define their own roles and permissions

ops.question: Do outside parties (customers, clients, vendors) use the app directly?

options.label: They open a secure link (no account needed)
They have their own accounts and log in

ops.question: Is this for one business, or will many separate businesses use it with their data kept apart?

options.label: Many separate businesses, each seeing only its own data

ops.question: How do additional people get access?
How do people sign in?
What happens when two people edit the same thing at once?

options.label: Common; the app must prevent or merge conflicting edits

ops.question: Do you need a record of who changed what and when?

options.label: Just created/updated by whom and when
A full, viewable history of every change

ops.question: How does the app reach people when something happens?

options.label: It doesn't — people check the app

ops.question: Must it work without internet?

options.label: Keeps working offline and syncs later

ops.question: Where is it used?

options.label: In a browser, on desktop and phone
In a browser, mostly on phones

ops.question: Do you start with existing data?
Do people need to get their data out?
When something is deleted, what really happens?

options.label: It's archived and can be restored
Records are never deleted, only voided/cancelled

ops.question: How much data will there be?
Does it need to connect to other tools?

options.label: A few key ones (e.g., accounting, payments, calendar)
Many — it needs a public API / webhooks

ops.question: Languages and regions?
Do some actions need someone else's approval first?
Must anything happen automatically on a schedule?

options.label: Records get created automatically (recurring invoices, appointments, reports)

ops.question: Does it hold data with special legal handling (health, payment cards, minors)?
How long is data kept?

options.label: Each business sets its own policy

ops.question: Can each business customize the app?

options.label: No — everyone gets the same thing

ops.question: What do people need to see across many records?

options.label: A dashboard with totals and counts

ops.question: When an uploaded spreadsheet has some invalid or unparseable rows, what happens?

options.label: Reject the whole file until fixed
Import valid rows, list rejected ones
Import everything, flag suspect rows for review

ops.question: Can a month that the Accountant marked reviewed (and locked per r7) be reopened for edits?

options.label: Only the Accountant can reopen it
Reopen allowed, keeping a versioned record of changes

ops.question: How are negative net profit, zero lines, and cent rounding handled in figures and KPIs?

options.label: Keep exact cents, show losses as negatives
Round to whole dollars for display
Round on import and store rounded

ops.question: When the Owner and Bookkeeper edit the same Revenue/Expense line at once, what happens?

options.label: Lock the line while one edits
Warn and require re-confirm on conflict

ops.question: What happens to budgets and expense lines when a Department is deleted or reorganized?

options.label: Block deletion while it has budgets/costs
Require reassigning them to another department
Archive department, keep historical lines attached

ops.question: How is a Cash Balance's 'as of date' and month attribution handled across timezones/month-end?

options.label: Date-only in the business's single timezone
Store timestamps in UTC, display local
Attribute strictly by calendar month of the date

ops.question: Can a Manager's per-department view (r2) be extended, e.g. delegated or cross-department access?

options.label: Managers can delegate temporary view access

ops.question: If the same month's spreadsheet is uploaded twice in quick succession (double-click/retry), how is it treated?

options.label: Each upload replaces prior per r5
Detect identical file and ask to confirm
Skip if identical to last import

ops.rationale: stated in the description: Four distinct actors log in with different powers.
stated in the description: r1 gives Owner/Bookkeeper edit rights and Managers/Accountant read-only.
stated in the description: It's an internal dashboard for one business ('our' excel files).
stated in the description: Core flow is uploading Excel financial files (a1, n8).
stated in the description: Explicitly an internal dashboard with totals, KPIs, and summaries.
stated in the description: g2 excludes bank/accounting-software connections.
stated in the description: r6 mandates a single currency (USD), no mixed currencies.
stated in the description: a11: Accountant exports Monthly Financials as Excel.

sheet.one_liner: internal dashboard based on our excel files with financials

actors.name: Owner
actors.description: Business owner who reviews overall financial health and trends.

actors.name: Bookkeeper
actors.description: Maintains the source spreadsheets and updates monthly figures.

actors.name: Manager
actors.description: Department lead who views budgets and actuals for their area.

actors.name: Accountant
actors.description: External advisor who reviews numbers at period close.

nouns.name: Monthly Financials
nouns.description: A month's summary of income, expenses, and profit pulled from the spreadsheet.

nouns.name: Revenue Line
nouns.description: A single income category for a period.

nouns.name: Expense Line
nouns.description: A single cost category for a period.

nouns.name: Budget
nouns.description: Planned amount for a category over a period.

nouns.name: Department
nouns.description: A part of the business that owns certain budgets and costs.
nouns.example: Sales, managed by J. Rivera, CC-200

nouns.name: Cash Balance
nouns.description: Running cash position as of a date.

nouns.name: KPI
nouns.description: A tracked metric shown on the dashboard.

nouns.name: Spreadsheet Import
nouns.description: A record of an uploaded Excel file and when it was loaded.

actions.example: Bookkeeper uploads financials_Mar2024.xlsx on Apr 2
Bookkeeper corrects Product Sales to $58,000
Bookkeeper adds Rent expense of $8,500
Bookkeeper records $142,300 as of Mar 31
Owner opens March 2024 summary
Owner checks gross margin against target
Manager reviews Marketing budget vs actuals
Manager opens Sales department costs
Owner sets Q2 Marketing budget to $16,000
Accountant reviews March figures at close
Accountant downloads March summary as Excel
Owner compares gross margin across quarters

rules.text: Only the Owner and Bookkeeper may upload or edit spreadsheet figures; Managers and Accountant see read-only views.
rules.example: A Manager cannot change an Expense Line amount.

rules.text: Each Manager may only view budgets and costs for their own Department.
rules.example: The Sales manager cannot open Operations department costs.

rules.text: A month's financials cannot be finalized until income and expense lines are both present.
rules.example: March cannot close while expenses are blank.

rules.text: Net profit must always equal total income minus total expenses for the same month.
rules.example: March net profit shows $22,700 = $84,200 - $61,500.

rules.text: Uploading a new spreadsheet for an already-loaded month replaces the prior figures and keeps a record of both uploads.
rules.example: Re-uploading March keeps the Apr 2 and Apr 5 import records.

rules.text: All amounts are shown in a single currency (USD) and no mixed currencies are allowed.
rules.example: A EUR figure would be rejected on import.

rules.text: Historical months cannot be edited once the Accountant marks them reviewed.
rules.example: Once March is reviewed, its lines lock.

rules.text: There may be only one Monthly Financials record per calendar month, and each Spreadsheet Import must carry a unique file name and month-covered identifier.
Every upload, figure edit, budget change, and review action is recorded with who did it and when, and these records cannot be altered or deleted.
Every Revenue Line, Expense Line, and Budget must reference a valid existing month/period and (where applicable) an existing Department; no orphaned lines are allowed.
Required fields (month, category, and amount) must be provided before a Revenue Line, Expense Line, or Cash Balance is saved.
Users interact with financial figures only through the dashboard; direct access to the underlying spreadsheets or data store is not permitted.
A Department cannot be deleted while it still has linked Budgets or Expense Lines assigned to it.

non_goals.text: Does not send or generate customer invoices.
Does not connect directly to bank accounts or accounting software.
Does not run payroll or process payments.
Does not forecast or project future financials automatically.
